title: World Cup Numbers
text:
Introduction
We all know FIFA is one of the biggest sporting events in the world. Working with a sports newsletter, we are creating a small public website to share the history of the men’s FIFA World Cup.
Some of the pages that we will be looking at includes:

Matches and Goals: how the number of matches and goals has changed over time
Crowds and Champions: attendance at each tournament and who won

AI tools that I used: None. I main use lecture notes, qtm 151 and prior assignments as reference. However, to make sure everything is accurate prior to executing, I entered everything in an ipynb environment first. I had a lot of issues debugging prior and I don’t want that to be the case. For the bonus tasks, I searched up on Google Gemini for reference.

title: Matches and Goals
text:
We use Figure 1 to plot number of matches played at each World Cup with thetotal goals scored. Graphically, we can see that the tournaments with more matches typically have more goals, suggesting a higher chance to score with every additional match played.

plt.scatter(cups["matches"], cups["goals"])
plt.xlabel("# of matches played")
plt.ylabel("# of total goals scored")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Matches Played vs. Total Goals Scored/World Cup (1930 to 2022)

title: Crowds and Champions
text:
Figure 1 refers toi total attendance at each World Cup (in thousands) from 1930 to 2022.

plt.plot(cups["year"], cups["attendance_k"])
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Total attendance (thousands)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Total World Cup Attendance Over Time (thousands)





The dataset covers 22 tournaments, and Brazil won 5 of them.
